---
title: "Research"
description: "Research interests in analytic number theory and Diophantine equations."
---

My research lies in analytic number theory, with an emphasis on the Hardy--Littlewood circle method and its applications to Diophantine equations. A recurring theme is to understand when local solubility predicts the existence and distribution of integral solutions.

## Current interests

### Forms in many variables

I study quantitative forms of the Hasse principle for homogeneous and weighted-homogeneous equations. This includes problems in which groups of variables occur with different weights and problems in which the coefficient vector is restricted to a thin set.

### Exponential sums and the circle method

My work uses estimates for exponential sums, mean-value methods, and geometric information about singular loci to control the minor arcs. On the major arcs, I study the singular series and singular integral that encode the local densities.

### Additive and combinatorial applications

I am also interested in Diophantine systems arising from combinatorial configurations, including multimagic squares and magic squares of powers.

## Further directions

Related interests include arithmetic statistics, sieve methods, additive combinatorics, and exponential-sum estimates beyond classical polynomial settings.
